utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any of the Defence team that disagrees with this, particularly the Nikolic Defence team? Go ahead, Mr. Acimovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. Can I please repeat what I actually said once already?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When Drago told me, "If you are not able to put a group of men together for that person [as interpreted] then you have to do it personally, you and your associates." I believe that he wanted to put additional pressure on me when he said that. He wanted me to take things really seriously, and allocate some of my men for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any of the Defence teams that wish to comment on this? And you can proceed, Mr. Nicholls, with your next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would note that on line 9 on previous page, "Mr. Nikolic" should read "Mr. Nicholls".

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know if there are any objections to that on your part, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, following this conversation at approximately 7.00 a.m. that you've just described with Drago Nikolic, did you discuss this conversation with anyone, what he had told you? Now talking about the 7.00 a.m. conversation when you said, "You've got to put together this squad, you should do it yourself if you can't put the men together." Did you discuss that conversation with anybody?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO ACIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke to my two associates. We consulted each other and a conclusion was that I should again try and get in touch with the Chief of Staff and that I should inform him about the orders that I had been given. But despite all that, I emphasise again we had firmly decided not to allocate any men for that task, and that we would personally not be involved, not a single soldier of my unit would get involved in those things. In other words, we would not carry out the order that we had been given. I called the duty operations officer again. I asked to be put through at any cost to the Chief of Staff. I assumed at the time, I suspected that there was a way of getting in touch with him. I asked the duty operations officer to talk to the chief himself if he could, to get back to me if possible and things like that. I also informed the duty operations officer about the situation. I notified him, but he couldn't be of any assistance. I've already told you that he sounded afraid and confused to me. I realised that he could not help me in any way with that matter. After that, I consulted my associates, I gave them certain tasks relative to the combat readiness of the unit. If there was an attack while I was absent, I made sure that everything would be put in place in order to avoid any surprises. After all that, at 9.00 or maybe 10.00, I went to Rocevic on my own, to see what Drago wanted from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Who was at the school when you got to Rocevic school? Who did you see there?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO ACIMOVIC
utterances.text: Down there, I met up with Vujadin Popovic. In other words, Drago wasn't there. He wasn't waiting for me down there, although he had promised he would be there. Instead of him, I met up with Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: As best you remember, exactly where did you meet up with Vujadin Popovic at the school? Outside? Inside? Can you describe that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO ACIMOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that we met up in front of the school. He told me to get into the school, to one of the offices there. I have to tell you that the school was open, the door was open. We went to one of the offices on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, you talked about being informed that there were shootings going on at the school. Did you see any corpses or injured people when you went to the school that morning around 10.00?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO ACIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I arrived down there, the chaos had progressed. There were a lot more unknown people, unfamiliar faces, in the school-yard. Also, as I was passing by, I saw that there were some dead bodies, corpses, lying around on the grass in front of the school bathroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you can tell us, if you remember, approximately how many corpses did you see on the grass there?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO ACIMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't give you a precise answer to that question, but I think that there may have been at least a dozen corpses lying around.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, thank you. You talked -- you stated that you went into one of the offices on the first floor with Mr. Popovic. What happened next? What transpired in the office?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO ACIMOVIC
utterances.text: Already in the school courtyard, he had started shouting, as soon as we met. He kept on asking me why I did not bring any men? And this continued while we were climbing up the stairs to that office. He also started putting pressure on me. He was swearing a lot. He kept on asking me why I hadn't brought any soldiers with me, the soldiers that had been requested from me. He started threatening me that I would be held responsible for not carrying out an order. The conversation continued, i.e., his threats continued. I told him that during the previous night I had told it very loud and clear that I would not allocate people for that purpose and that he could do whatever he wanted as far as I was concerned and I repeated that I would not allocate any soldier for that purpose, nor would I participate in anything contained in that order. He started swearing again. He reminded me that -- and he said it in approximately these words, "Fuck you. Do you know what happened to the Serbs in Kravica and other Serb villages which were torched and which are around Srebrenica?" I told him, "Yes, I know. I know what happened there, because I am one of the rare people who went to help those villagers. I went there to help them when this was going on. I'm well familiar with the situation. I know what happened to these villagers but that has nothing to do with what you are requesting me to do." I told him then, "No matter what the price will be to pay, I am not going to be involved. I'm not going to participate in any of that." During that conversation, he left the office, he gave instructions to some of his soldiers, of the soldiers who were down there, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, during this -- I'll call it a conversation, but this difficult situation you were in, in this office in the school, was there anybody else present or was it just you and Vujadin Popovic? Is there anybody else present around there listening to this or observing this exchange?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO ACIMOVIC
utterances.text: It is possible that there was somebody, some of his soldiers, but I'm not sure. I don't know whether there was anybody there, whether any of his soldiers were there. I assume that there were but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And did he tell you to do anything else, to do anything else because you had said you were not going to provide men from your battalion?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO ACIMOVIC
utterances.text: Cursing all the time and swearing all the time, he told me that it was just impossible that none of my men wanted to take part in all that. I also told him, and I asked him whether he was aware of the situation that my unit was, the unit that I had left in my defence sector. An attack could have ensued any moment from the rear of our lines. I told him that. I also told him that I had to go back to my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And what did Mr. Popovic do then, if anything, to take care of the problem that there weren't any people there willing to take part in the executions? What did he do?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO ACIMOVIC
utterances.text: He was putting pressure on me all this time. He continued doing so. He insisted on me trying to go down there, to talk to somebody, to talk to somebody in the school-yard, as there were a lot of different soldiers there. I've already told you that I saw them as I was coming in. I told him I wouldn't do that, that I would not ask anybody to do any such thing. He kept on insisting. He literally forced me to go down to the school-yard and to see whether there was anybody, any individual, who wanted, who was willing to take part in all that. I did that. I went downstairs, but I was adamant in my mind that I would not ask any of the men who were present there. I remember that somebody approached me and asked me what was going on, and I just told that person, within that context, what the lunatics were asking for me to do. And this is exactly what I called them and I told that person that I would not take part in any of that thing. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I hate to interrupt the testimony of the witness. I, just for the record, feel it is important to note that as of page 50, we've entered into the material which was disclosed by the witness on Sunday. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you did not interrupt the witness any way. He had finished his -- let's proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to go into an area now with some names that I'll be going into. I would request that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, if we go into private session I'll give the basis --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I've just asked if there is any objection. Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We would like to know the basis for the OTP to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls, can you explain, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to go into private session to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Let's go into private session to do that. [Part of Private Session made public by order of Trial Chamber]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't think there is any reason for the witness to leave but if my friends want the witness to leave - I'm hearing some static from over there - that's fine, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you understand English, Mr. Acimovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I'll ask you to remove your -- yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Just for a point of clarification, there may be names that will be in Serbian that he will understand so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So I think he best leaves the courtroom. There don't need to be at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: But just so I can say, these are the names that I'm going to refer to that are contained in the supplemental information sheet that has been provided to the Defence. So there's no mystery there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They don't need to be mentioned now at this stage while we are discussing whether we should in private session for the next part of the testimony or not. One moment. Mr. Meek, Mr. Bourgon? I don't know. I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think I can clear this up possibly very simply without anybody needing to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Do sit down, please. But don't put your headphones on. Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Maybe at this stage, Mr. President, I can inform the Trial Chamber that I would, for once, agree with the Prosecution that we go into private session. The reason being is that the names that he will mention are potential Defence witnesses, since yesterday. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I imagined I would have expected from you. But Mr. Meek is objecting so we have got a conflicting approach here. Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Judge, I didn't object. I just asked for the basis to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. Go ahead with your explanation first and then we will --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon has essentially said it, that there are names of persons present who will be discussed who are still living in the area, and for the sake of those persons, whether they -- who may be witnesses, now I hear for the Defence or for anybody, they may require protective measures and we would destroy that by going through this in open session, so it's for the sake of these persons, potentially, who need it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Would you endorse Mr. Bourgon's position?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I think the witness can put on his headphones again. Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I'd like -- the names should be in private session, but the testimony that goes along with the name doesn't have to be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I was going to say that to the extent that some of the events and positions of these people would possibly reveal them to other people who were present whose names I'm not going to use so I can't -- I honesty cannot say where the line is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we can't say either because we haven't heard the testimony as yet so I think we'll play it by the ear and at any time you have reservations, Mr. Bourgon, and would like any part of the testimony to be in public, in open session, you will let us know and we can repeat the question and the answer in open session. Agreed? Agreed? Thank you. So let's proceed in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, when you went back into the office, after having gone outside -- we are in private session now, witness, and what that means is that nobody outside the courtroom can hear what we're saying and they won't be able to read it later or see it. It stays within the courtroom. What was going on in the office when you went back inside? Had any volunteers appeared? Or what was going on when you went back into the office?

utterances.speaker: SRECKO ACIMOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let me clear this up. I have already noted that Popovic went in and out of the office, where I remained waiting for him to come back. At that moment, Your Honour, he again pressurised me, exerted pressure on me to take part in this, to get involved, and I refused to and I said that I had to go back to my unit, for all the reasons that I've already mentioned. I explained to him again about the status of the unit, and explosions could be heard at that time, and they were -- the sound was coming from the sector manned by my unit, and I said, "I have to go back to my unit." And he told me, "Wait just a moment." And he took -- I'm sorry, I have to add one thing that I failed to mention earlier. During this conversation, I said that he had to evacuate these men from Rocevici, from the school there, that the school building was not to be used for this purpose, it's a building where children go to get education, and that those prisoners that we were talking about had to be evacuated from Rocevici, and that if that is not done, there was the danger that the soldiers from my unit who were from Rocevici might abandon their positions. Because one of those companies, two companies, in fact, in those companies that I've already mentioned, the soldiers were from Rocevici, and the news had reached them about the wounding of this woman, and it had caused general chaos on the front line. I explained all that to Popovic, that some of the units, some people from the unit might abandon their positions and that I would not be held responsible for something like that, if that should happen, in light of the fact that he was keeping me there in the school. What I want to tell you is we had this conversation, if you could call it a conversation, there was a lot of cursing, threats, things of that nature, and then he took the civilian telephone, he picked it up, and I think he called the duty officer, and he told him that vehicles should be sent to Rocevici urgently. Before that I had told him that these men should be evacuated or taken back to where they came from, and as for any of the villages in my defence sector, or rather that he should evacuate those people from Rocevici and I proposed to him the barracks in Kozluk because there were conditions there to accommodate the prisoners, and I repeated that several times. He called the brigade and he asked for the vehicles to be sent to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have to leave it there today. We'll continue tomorrow. The sitting is in the afternoon. Yes it's only Friday that we have the sitting in the morning. So at 2.15 tomorrow. Mr. Acimovic, I need to make something very clear to you. Between today and until you finish your testimony, you're not to communicate with anyone or allow anyone to communicate with you, discuss the subject matter of your testimony. At this point in time, you're not to communicate with anybody on the subject matter. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We stand adjourned until tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
